requirements.CORE-BUILD-001: The build writes a script-tag bundle to `dist/bio.viz-{version}/bio.viz.js` that defines the global `BioViz`.
requirements.CORE-BUILD-002: The build writes an ES module bundle to `dist/bio.viz-{version}/bio.viz.esm.js` with the same exports as the script-tag bundle.
requirements.CORE-API-001: `version` equals the `version` field of package.json: in the source, in both committed bundles, and as `BioViz.version` on a page that loads the script-tag bundle.
requirements.CORE-DEP-001: package.json declares no runtime dependencies: safety.viz and webR are loaded beside the bundle on a page and are never bundled into it.
requirements.CORE-SITE-001: The site's home page names the library and its version, and shows the version reported by the bundle that page loaded.
requirements.CORE-SITE-002: The site's home page holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll.
requirements.CORE-DATA-001: The synthetic biomarker study is vendored as three files in `site/data/synthetic-study/` (`synthetic_results.csv`, `synthetic_participants.csv`, `synthetic_outcomes.csv`) with a source record, `SOURCE.json`, beside them that names the gsm.bio repository, the commit the files were copied from and each file's path there.
requirements.CORE-DATA-002: Each vendored file matches its entry in the source record: the SHA-256 checksum, the size in bytes, the column names and the row count. A file that is changed, missing, or present but not recorded fails the check, as does a record edited without its file.
requirements.CORE-DATA-003: The results table has the columns `USUBJID`, `VISIT`, `VISITNUM`, `TEST`, `STRESU`, `STRESN` and 11,472 rows, one per participant, biomarker and visit: 200 participants, twelve biomarkers, and the visits Baseline, Week 2, Week 4, Week 8 and Week 12.
requirements.CORE-DATA-004: The participant table has the columns `USUBJID`, `ARM`, `SEX`, `AGE`, `BMIBL`, `RESPONSE` and 200 rows, one per participant, and every participant in the results table is in it.
requirements.CORE-DATA-005: The outcomes table has the columns `USUBJID`, `PARAMCD`, `PARAM`, `AVAL`, `CNSR` and 200 rows, one per participant and endpoint, and every participant in it is in the participant table.
requirements.CORE-DATA-006: Vendoring is a copy: each file is written exactly as gsm.bio holds it at the recorded commit, with the checksum of those bytes recorded. Nothing is retyped, reordered or regenerated, and a second check fails when a vendored file differs from gsm.bio's file at that commit.
requirements.CORE-SITE-003: The gallery page lists every chart the registry marks available, each with links to its evidence page and its API reference. When no chart is available it says that no chart is published yet.
requirements.CORE-SITE-004: The gallery page lists the library's shared parts, each with links to its evidence page and its API reference.
requirements.CORE-SITE-005: Every module in the registry (`site/config.json`) says whether it is a chart or a shared part and names its requirement matrix and its API reference. The site build refuses an entry that does not.
requirements.CORE-SITE-006: Each module has an evidence page that lists every requirement in its matrix with the requirement's text, the tests named for it and the result each test recorded. A requirement with no test says so.
requirements.CORE-SITE-007: An evidence page shows, under a requirement, each screenshot a test captured for it. The site build fails when the evidence set names a screenshot that is not committed.
requirements.CORE-SITE-008: An evidence page says when its results were recorded and in what environment, and links the continuous-integration run when there was one.
requirements.CORE-SITE-009: Each module has an API reference page rendered from the module's one reference file in `docs/`: its headings, paragraphs, lists, tables and code, with a list of its sections at the top.
requirements.CORE-SITE-010: The site build fails when an API reference has drifted from the code: an export of the bundle that no reference documents, a function a reference documents that the bundle does not export, a parameter documented in the source that the reference leaves out, or a constant whose value the reference does not give.
requirements.CORE-SITE-011: Every requirement row has at least one test named for it, and no test names a requirement that is in no matrix. The evidence run fails otherwise.
requirements.CORE-SITE-012: The gallery page holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll.
requirements.CORE-SITE-013: A module's evidence page holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll.
requirements.CORE-SITE-014: A module's API reference page holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll; a table is restacked as a list rather than scrolled sideways.
requirements.CORE-SITE-015: The site publishes the vendored synthetic study at `data/synthetic-study/` with its source record, and the gallery page says what each table holds, how many rows it has and which gsm.bio commit it was copied from.
requirements.CORE-VAR-001: A variable is written one way wherever one is taken, an axis, a group, a colour or a panel: a biomarker at a visit with a value type, `{ measure, visit, value }`, or a column, `{ col }`. The value types are `raw`, `baseline`, `change`, `fold_change` and `percent_change`, and `raw` when none is given. `variable()` returns the variable in full.
requirements.CORE-VAR-002: A malformed variable is refused with a message that names what is wrong: not an object, neither or both of a biomarker and a column, an empty name, a value type that is not one of the five, a missing visit, a visit given with a baseline value, or a key that is not known.
requirements.CORE-VAR-003: A variable that asks for a cut is refused with a message saying that the cut rule is not available yet.
requirements.CORE-VAR-004: The value type `raw` is the participant's result for the biomarker at the visit, as the results table holds it.
requirements.CORE-VAR-005: The value type `baseline` is the participant's result at the baseline visits named in settings. With several named, one result per visit is brought to one value by their mean, or by the statistic named in settings (`min`, `max`, `first`); with none named, the first visit in visit order is the baseline.
requirements.CORE-VAR-006: The value type `change` is the result at the visit minus the baseline. A participant with no result at the visit, or no baseline result, has no change and is dropped and counted.
requirements.CORE-VAR-007: The value type `fold_change` is the result at the visit divided by the baseline. A participant whose baseline is zero or negative has no fold change and is dropped and counted.
requirements.CORE-VAR-008: The value type `percent_change` is one hundred times the change divided by the baseline. A participant whose baseline is zero or negative has no percent change and is dropped and counted.
requirements.CORE-VAR-009: `label()` names a variable in words, for an axis title or a legend: the column's name, or the biomarker, its visit and its value type.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-001: `frame()` resolves named variables to one record per participant: the participant's id, under the name of the id column, and one field per variable, named as the caller named it. Participants are in the participant table's order when one is given, and otherwise in the order first seen in the results.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-002: On the synthetic study the frame for IL-6 change from Baseline to Week 4 has 186 participants and 14 dropped: 13 with no result at Week 4 and one whose result there is missing.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-003: A participant for whom a variable cannot be worked out is left out of the frame and counted, by reason and by variable. Every participant seen is in the frame or counted once: under the first variable, in the order given, that could not be worked out.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-004: Only the results table is required. With it alone the frame resolves a biomarker variable and holds no participant column.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-005: A column variable is read from the participant table when that table is given and has the column, and otherwise from a column carried on the results rows.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-006: A wide table with one row per participant needs no special handling: given as the results table, or as the participant table, each of its columns resolves as a column variable.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-007: Of several results for one participant, biomarker and visit, the first usable one in table order is used, and each later one is counted as an unused row.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-008: A result that is missing or not a number is not a result: the row is counted as unused, and a participant with no other result at the visit is dropped and counted. Text that reads as a number is a number.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-009: With a participant table given, it says who the participants are: a participant with results who is not in it is left out and counted, a participant in it with no result is dropped for a biomarker variable and counted, and a row with no id, or a second row for a participant, is counted as unused.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-010: A column read from the results rows must hold one value for the participant. A participant for whom it is empty, holds more than one value, or (for a column read as a number) is not a number is dropped and counted.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-011: By default every variable is required. A variable not named in the `required` setting is left empty (null) in a participant's record instead of dropping the participant.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-012: Column names are settings, named as safety.viz names them, and their defaults are the synthetic study's: `USUBJID`, `TEST`, `STRESN`, `VISIT`, `VISITNUM`, with the participant table's id column the same as the results table's unless named.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-013: A call that cannot be made is refused with a message naming what is wrong: tables that are not arrays of records, a table that is not one of the two, variables not given by name, a name that is the id column's, a setting that is not known or has a value it cannot take, or a column a setting names that the table does not have.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-014: The frame's records are plain text and finite numbers, and go to R through the connection as they are, the fields named as a statistics function takes them (`strValueCol`, `strGroupCol`).
requirements.CORE-FRAME-015: The frame changes nothing it is given: not the tables, the variables or the settings.
requirements.CORE-API-002: Both committed bundles export `core` (a page reads `BioViz.core`): `variable`, `frame`, `label`, and the vocabulary `VALUE_TYPES`, `BASELINE_STATS`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `DROPPED` and `UNUSED`.
requirements.CORE-BUILD-003: The core module imports nothing from outside `src/core/`, and reaches for no page, no chart and no network.
requirements.CORE-FRAME-016: `visits()` lists the visits of a results table in visit order: by the visit-order column when the table has one and otherwise by name with numbers counted as numbers, and only the visits with at least one usable result.
requirements.CORE-MAN-001: Both committed bundles export `portfolio` (a page reads `BioViz.portfolio`): the chart list, equal to `src/data/portfolio.json`, in safety.viz's portfolio manifest format, version 2.
requirements.CORE-MAN-002: The chart list validates against safety.viz's portfolio manifest schema at the recorded commit, and a list that breaks the format does not.
requirements.CORE-MAN-003: The schema is safety.viz's `src/data/schema/portfolio.json`, copied byte for byte to `src/data/schema/` by `tools/vendor-portfolio-schema.mjs`, with a record naming safety.viz's `dev` branch, the commit and the file's checksum and size; `npm test` fails when the file and its record disagree, and continuous integration compares the file with safety.viz at the recorded commit (`npm run portfolio:check-source`).
requirements.CORE-MAN-004: The chart list has one entry for each chart `site/config.json` marks available, and no other, keyed by its module, under its title and the name of the function the bundle exports for it; each entry names `bio.viz` as its library and the declared group `biomarkers` as its group, and takes the results table from the labs and vitals domain, required, and the participant table from the subject-level domain, optional.
requirements.CORE-MAN-005: Each entry's settings are exactly its chart's column-name settings (the keys of its `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` ending in `_col` or carrying `_col_`), each with the chart's default and required exactly where the chart refuses `null` for it; `participant_id_col`, whose default `null` means `id_col`'s name, reads `id_col`'s standard column from the subject-level domain; and an unmapped setting is left out (`unmappedSettings: "omit"`).
requirements.CORE-MAN-006: An export a module lists in `api.data` is documented under one heading of its own, and its fields are not held to the reference one by one; the core lists `portfolio` there.
requirements.CORE-MAN-007: The site publishes the chart list at `portfolio.json`, the same list a page that loads the bundle reads as `BioViz.portfolio`, and the format it names at `schema/portfolio.json`.
